bull.b: Alnylam’s commercial franchise is scaling rapidly, led by AMVUTTRA and broader TTR adoption. Sustained growth across U.S. and international markets can expand operating leverage, strengthen prescriber penetration, and support recurring product revenue.

The shift from historical losses to meaningful earnings and cash generation improves financial flexibility. High free-cash-flow conversion can fund clinical development, commercialization, and partnerships while reducing reliance on external capital.

A diversified RNAi pipeline and targeted partnerships broaden future growth beyond the current franchise. Geographic commercialization and AI-enabled discovery may improve patient identification, development efficiency, and the durability of the platform.

bear.b: The guidance reduction shows that initial launch dynamics were unusually strong and may not persist at the same pace. Normalizing switch demand raises execution risk and makes future growth increasingly dependent on first-line adoption and market expansion.

Higher royalty obligations transfer more of incremental product revenue to partners, limiting operating leverage as AMVUTTRA scales. Persistent margin dilution could reduce the cash contribution of the company’s fastest-growing commercial franchise.

The balance sheet is more stable after the profitability inflection, but leverage remains meaningful and the recent earnings base has limited history. If growth or margins normalize, debt obligations could constrain investment flexibility and amplify volatility.
